title: Quinvirinae Coverage Audit
h1: Does the apple stem pitting virus module actually work?
standfirst: Quinvirinae is the subfamily module covering Foveavirus, Robigovirus, Banmivirus, Ravavirus and Sustrivirus — apple stem pitting virus, cherry necrotic rusty mottle virus, and the woody-host relatives left after Carlavirus was split out. Same gene layout as Carlavirus: replicase, triple gene block, coat protein, nucleic-acid-binding protein.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Five genera that share a layout, separated from a sixth on measurement.

blocks.html: All six Quinvirinae genera share the replicase / triple-gene-block / coat protein layout, so the organisation rule alone would have kept Carlavirus with them. Routing separated them: lumped, 25 references reach 81.0%; split, this half reaches 98.0% and Carlavirus gained eleven points.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Its dump had to be re-fetched from scratch.

blocks.html: The working dump had been bulk-cleaned before this report was written, so the genome list was rebuilt from the class-wide table for the five genera and re-fetched: 9,505 features over 6,205 unique sequences.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Conventional, with the two alternative-frame ORFs at 30 and 40.

blocks.html: 400 for the replicase, 80 for the coat protein, 60 / 30 / 25 down the triple gene block. The accessories sit at 30–40, and §07 has a note about what that costs.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: 98.0% at the project budget — the best of the six backfilled modules.

blocks.html: The curve is 78% at 5 references and 98% at 25. These are woody-host viruses with comparatively deep sampling per species, so a small reference set goes a long way — the opposite of Carlavirus, which needs more than the budget allows.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Five essential features at 97.3–99.3%, three accessories below.

blocks.html: These accessory rates come from a 150-routed-genome run whose output is not on disk. The 108-genome quality run that is on disk gives P14 22.2%, ORF2a 29.6% and ORF5a 25.9%. The core-feature rates are not in question; the three accessory rates are, and §07 says so.
Every copy_num assignment in the shipped module was already correct. No change was needed.
Five of five core features essential and called on at least 97.3% of routed genomes.
10 flags are a missing essential feature, 8 are contigs with too many ambiguous bases, 3 are “too many HSPs”. There are no exact duplicate calls anywhere in the module.

sections.title: What it cannot do
sections.lede: Two documented architecture notes, one closed question, and one number still to reproduce.

blocks.html: ORF2a and ORF5a are called entirely inside TGB1 and CP — 100% of their calls. That is the architecture their names describe: ORF2a is an alternative reading frame overlapping ORF2, ORF5a overlaps ORF5. The collections are unrelated to their hosts (28% and 31% identity over about a quarter coverage), neither is essential, and nothing about this is a defect.

P14 is closed, 30 September 2026. Where it is called it sits inside the CP span — 92.5% and 89.6% containment on the two GRSPaV rep contigs, above the 80% floor that keeps the duplicate-call check from crying wolf over the routine short overlaps of a compact genome. It is not a profile calling someone else's gene. The two features share no detectable homology in either direction: blastp over 170 P14 × 915 CP collection members returns zero HSPs at E ≤ 1e-3; the best P14 profile scores 21.7 bits against a CP member and the best CP profile 22.4 bits against a P14 member, against cutoffs of 30 and 80; and the two proteins actually emitted at that locus — a 259 aa nucleocapsid protein and a 125 aa 14 kDa protein — align nowhere at all, not even at E ≤ 1000. What the coordinates show instead is an out-of-frame overlapping ORF: on ON868740, CP at 7847–8623 in frame +2 and p14 at 8277–8651 in frame +3; on KT000366, 7771–8547 (+2) and 8228–8584 (+3). Real variation, one protein encoded overlapping another, accepted by the curator as such. Neither feature is dropped and neither profile set is rebuilt; qc_duplicate_calls.py takes --expected P14:CP for this module. Nothing depends on it either way, because P14 carries no copy_num.

The earlier reading of this overlap was wrong and is worth recording as such. This section previously called it unexplained and offered two candidate causes — that CP's called span runs long, or that the P14 profile is promiscuous at bit_cutoff 30. Neither is the case. The frames settle it, and no window or cutoff needs touching. The inference that a nested call must mean one profile is misbehaving is the thing to distrust: in a compact viral genome it can equally mean the genes genuinely overlap, and only a homology measurement in both directions distinguishes the two.

P14's call rate is unreconciled and should be re-measured. §05's table reports 60.7% of 150 routed genomes (91 calls). The only measurement on disk is a 108-genome quality run, which gives 22.2% (24 calls) — cross-checked against that run's feature-count distribution, which accounts for all 24 exactly. The two disagree on ORF5a as well, 8.7% against 25.9%, so this is not a rounding difference and one of them is measuring a different population or is simply wrong. The 150-genome output is not on disk to check. The closure above does not rest on the rate — it rests on the frames and the absence of homology — but the rate should not be quoted from either source until one is reproduced.

One thing the on-disk run does show clearly is that the accessories are nearly mutually exclusive: 52 genomes carry the five core features and nothing else, 22 carry core + P14, 24 carry core + ORF2a + ORF5a, and exactly one carries all three. That is two accessory architectures inside one module rather than a gradient, and it is the kind of split that a single pooled call rate hides.
The evaluation is a sample — 150 genomes at ≥6 kb, seed 29. Routing in §04 is a census.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: No corrections, the open question closed, and one measurement to redo.

blocks.html: This module's copy_num was already right, which puts it with Carlavirus and Ampelovirus rather than with Velarivirus and Closterovirus. The P14 nesting was the only finding and it is now resolved rather than merely documented: measured in both directions, shown to be an out-of-frame overlapping ORF, and closed by the curator as real variation. No feature was dropped and no profile set was rebuilt. P14 carries no copy_num, so genomes without it are not flagged for missing it — quality2.tsv reports zero ‘missing essential feature: 14 kDa protein’ against 84 in the pre-correction quality.tsv. The same architecture appears once more in the module: ORF2a is called 100% inside TGB1, out of frame, on KT000366 — still flagged, on the same reasoning but not yet the same decision. One measurement is left open: P14's call rate, which §05 and the on-disk quality run do not agree on.

Eight of eight features have profiles and five are essential on measurement. P14's nesting is measured, explained and closed — an out-of-frame overlapping ORF, no homology with CP in either direction, nothing depending on it. Its call rate is the one number here still to be reproduced.

The smallest collapse ratio of the six backfilled modules, and that is a fact about the source rather than the module: these genera are annotated comparatively consistently, so there was less duplication to remove. The module's vocabulary is complete after eleven genomes; the source is still climbing at 150.
